messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] runtime-serving: p99 latency spike + throughput drop detected for release-hotpath. Started ~2378001200. p99 x4 baseline, throughput -30%. Auto-opened INC-20237. Paging eng-oncall and eng-runtime.
maya: paging @oncall and @eng-runtime — are we seeing customer-facing errors? :rotating_light:
raj: I pushed a kernel-selection change (kernsel_v2) in the release rollout (v1.23.3). Canary at 5%. Early telemetry shows a mismatched kernel combo on a subset of GPU types; the runtime is falling back to the generic kernel path which is significantly slower for our hotpath.
raj: logs:
```
2026-03-15T15:07:21Z ERROR kernel_selector: preferred=fused_conv_v2, selected=generic_conv, reason=missing_kernel
2026-03-15T15:07:21Z WARN runtime: KV cache cold start + fallback path taken, batch_size=1, latency=1200ms
```
elena: assigning SRE lead. @samir you good to take incident lead? we'll follow the runbook for postdeploy regressions.
samir: taking it. Oncall handover: samir -> I'm watching. First ask: can we immediately stop new kernel routing or flip canary to 0%? We should minimize customer impact while debugging.
raj: yes. Two immediate options:
- flip feature flag: `redwoodctl feature disable kernsel_v2 --env=prod` (preferred)
- reduce canary weight: `trafficctl set runtime-serving --version=v1.23.3 --weight=0.0`
I'll prepare the rollout revert now.
maya: are there any customers timing out? liz, can you pull impact list from support dashboard?
liz: pulling. Initial look: AcmeCorp and BrightMetrics have elevated 5xx and timeouts on long requests. Estimated affected pct ~2% of overall requests, but skewed to high-qps customers. Links: https://dash.redwood/internal/runtime/INC-20237
oncall-bot: Handoff note: user samir accepted. Notifying secondary responder: raj. Incident channel: INC-20237 created.
raj: executing feature flip now. Command:
```
$ redwoodctl feature disable kernsel_v2 --env=prod --actor=raj
Feature "kernsel_v2" disabled (scope: prod)
```
raj: also temporarily increasing kernel affinity timeout to force older kernel path to remain preferred while we stabilize:
```
$ redwoodctl config set runtime.kernel_affinity.prefer_old=1 --env=prod
```
elena: monitoring metrics. Tell me when p99 starts falling.
(monitoring noises)
maya: p99 for release-hotpath: 4.2s -> 1.1s within 3 minutes of flip. Throughput recovering but still 10% below baseline. Error rate trending down.
samir: good. Next: we should rollback the rollout artifact and schedule a fix. raj, can you confirm whether this is a missing kernel artifact on specific HW (A100-p4 / older driver)?
raj: yes. Root cause appears to be missing fused kernels for older driver combos. The selection logic preferred them, but fallback path has large overhead and interacts poorly with our batching heuristics (batcher immediately sends small batches leading to high per-token overhead).
raj: snippet showing batcher behavior:
```
info batcher: batch_interval_ms=2, observed_mean_batch=1.2, preferred_batch_path=fused_conv_v2
```
samir: mitigation steps agreed:
1) disable kernsel_v2 (done)
2) reduce canary to 0 and rollback config (in progress)
3) revert batching param change that interacts badly with fallback
4) identify affected HW/drivers and mark them in model manifest to avoid fused kernels until next deploy
5) run a focused canary in a dev region
elena: I'll open an incident ticket and notify CS for proactive outreach to AcmeCorp and BrightMetrics. We should offer mitigation window and status.
liz: drafting customer note. ETA 20m. We have a small number of timed-out requests but no data loss reported. We'll proactively reach out to top impacted customers.
raj: starting quick config rollback and restart of runtime pods on a limited subset:
```
$ kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/runtime-serving --to-revision=23
$ kubectl -n runtime rollout status deployment/runtime-serving
```
oncall-bot: auto: rollback job queued by raj at 2378001505.
maya: are we comfortable with full rollback? Any reason to keep the new kernels blocked while we do a controlled fix/patch?
samir: full rollback with kernel selection disabled. We'll ship a targeted patch that adds driver->kernel capability check before preferring fused kernels. Ownership: raj, priority P0.
raj: ack. I'll push a small guard and run unit + integration canaries in staging.
elena: monitoring update: p99 stabilized to 200ms within 12 minutes of rollback, throughput at -2% (within acceptable noise). Flagging incident as mitigated for customer-facing impact. We'll keep the incident open for postmortem.
maya: postmortem owners: raj (root cause/fix), elena (operational runbook gaps), liz (customer comms). Action items assigned in INC-20237.
samir: adding one extra action: add automated test to canary harness that validates kernel availability matrix for each GPU/driver combo.
maya: thanks everyone. We'll do handoff to night oncall at 2378001834: @oncall-bot note created.
oncall-bot: Handoff complete. Night oncall: kira.
liz: customer note sent to affected accounts. Support queue updated.
raj: will follow up with PR link and CI results; aiming to have fix out before next deployment window.
elena: closing note: no SLA breach expected; monitoring for regressions. Postmortem to be scheduled tomorrow. :thumbsup:
maya: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem: INC-20237-PM tracking.
